documents.title: Cardiac rehabilitation discharge
documents.author: cardiac rehabilitation
documents.body: Cardiac rehabilitation program, discharge summary 01/12/2024. Referred after NSTEMI and LAD stent (10/2023). Completed the program, missing a few sessions over the holidays. Exercise capacity improved steadily on the bike and treadmill at low incline; knees limited incline work. No angina or arrhythmia during sessions. Resting blood pressure and heart rate at goal on metoprolol. Education: diet, medications, warning symptoms. Home plan: walk 30-40 minutes most days, add light resistance work.

documents.title: Office Visit - follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, 3.5 months after NSTEMI/LAD stent. Finished cardiac rehab last week and is walking 30+ minutes daily, no chest pain, no dyspnea. No bleeding on aspirin and clopidogrel beyond easy bruising. Thirst and nocturia stable on amiloride, up once at night. CPAP nightly, feels the best he has in years. Mood good. Oncology surveillance CT and colonoscopy are next month.

Meds reviewed, no changes: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75 (through Oct 2024), metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, lithium 300 bid, amiloride 5, NTG prn (unused).

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. A few small bruises forearms.

A/P: CAD s/p PCI, stable. HTN at goal. Lithium/NDI: level, BMP, TSH, CBC today. OSA: adherent. Next visit physical in May.

reports.conclusion: Expected postsurgical change. No evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.

documents.title: Surveillance colonoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body: Outside gastroenterology. Procedure 02/27/2024. Indication: one year after right hemicolectomy for colon cancer. Aspirin continued; clopidogrel continued per cardiology, no biopsies planned unless needed. Prep excellent. Ileocolic anastomosis widely patent with healthy-appearing mucosa; neoterminal ileum normal. No polyps or masses throughout the remaining colon and rectum. Small internal hemorrhoids. Impression: normal post-hemicolectomy colonoscopy. Recommend repeat in 3 years (2027).

documents.title: Oncology surveillance - one year
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Medical oncology, 03/04/2024. One year after resection of stage IIA (pT3 N0) ascending colon adenocarcinoma, no adjuvant therapy. Interval NSTEMI 10/2023 treated with an LAD stent. Feels well, bowels regular, no bleeding, weight steady. Exam unremarkable. CEA 1.8. CT 02/12 without recurrence; colonoscopy 02/27 normal anastomosis, no polyps, repeat 2027. No evidence of disease. Plan: CEA and visit every 6 months through 2025, CT yearly through 2026.

documents.title: Chest pressure walking
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last few weeks I've had a pressure feeling in my chest going into my left arm on my morning walks. Lasts maybe 10 min, goes away if I stop and stand. Never when I'm sitting. Doesn't feel like October, much milder. I have a cardiology appt in May. Should I move it up?

documents.title: Call back re exertional chest pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called him. Episodes only with brisk walking, relieved by rest within about 10 minutes, none at rest, none waking him, no syncope. Has not used nitroglycerin. Stable pattern, so no ED today. Reviewed: if pain at rest, lasting over 15 min, or not relieved by NTG x1, call 911. I called the cardiology office: they moved him to 3/27 and will do stress testing. Advised walking at an easier pace until then.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up - angina
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, 03/27/2024.

Six months out from NSTEMI with mid-LAD drug-eluting stent. For several weeks he has had a pressure in the left chest spreading to the left arm on his morning walks, about ten minutes at a time, easing with rest. Nothing at rest. Has not taken nitroglycerin.

Meds: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 nightly, lithium carbonate 300 twice daily, amiloride 5. NKDA. Never smoker, social alcohol, office manager. Father MI at 55.

BP 135/85, HR 78. Examination unremarkable. ECG: sinus, no acute changes.

Regadenoson SPECT myocardial perfusion study (pharmacologic stress chosen because knee arthritis keeps him from adequate treadmill exercise): reversible perfusion defect of the anterior wall on stress images, normal perfusion at rest. Gated EF normal.

Assessment: stable angina pectoris from coronary artery disease, anterior ischemia, post LAD stent.
Plan: optimize medical therapy first. Increase metoprolol succinate to 50 mg daily. Add isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg every morning. Nitroglycerin SL as needed; sit down before using. Continue aspirin and clopidogrel. If symptoms persist despite this, we will proceed to angiography. Follow up in 3 months.

documents.title: Pharmacy - metoprolol duplicate
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy called: two metoprolol succinate strengths on file (25 from the hospital, 50 from cardiology). Confirmed with patient and cardiology letter that he takes 50 mg once daily now; 25 mg discontinued, pharmacy will inactivate it. Isosorbide filled without issue. Med list updated.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM, age 60 today-ish (birthday was last week).

Interval: angina on walks in March; cardiology found anterior ischemia on a regadenoson SPECT, raised metoprolol to 50 and added isosorbide. Since then he's had two brief episodes on hills, none in the last 3 weeks, no NTG needed. Some dull headaches the first week of isosorbide, now gone. Colon surveillance in Feb all clear, next colonoscopy 2027. Psychiatry visit due in the fall.

ROS: no dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations, GI bleeding, urinary change beyond baseline nocturia once. Knees same.

Meds: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75 (until Oct), metoprolol succinate 50, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30, NTG prn, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, lithium 300 bid, amiloride 5. NKDA.
Social: still office manager. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks a week. Walking daily.

EXAM: vitals as charted, BMI 27. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no bruit. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed laparoscopic scars. Extremities without edema, pulses intact. Skin: scattered ecchymoses forearms. Neuro nonfocal, no tremor. Mood euthymic. PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. CAD with MI 10/2023 s/p LAD stent, stable angina improving on medical therapy. Updated problem list: the MI is now historical. Continue current regimen; cardiology June.
2. HTN at goal.
3. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today on atorvastatin 40.
4. Bipolar I on lithium, lithium NDI on amiloride: lithium, CMP, TSH today.
5. OSA on CPAP, adherent.
6. Stage IIA colon cancer, NED, oncology following.
7. Health maintenance: Shingrix done, Tdap 2017, hep C/HIV done 2022. Flu and COVID in the fall. A1c today.

RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body: Outside cardiology, 06/26/2024. Stable angina after LAD stent, on metoprolol succinate 50 and isosorbide mononitrate 30 since March. No chest pressure since mid-April, walking daily at a moderate pace. No NTG use. Vitals reviewed. Exam unremarkable. Plan: continue medical therapy, no angiography needed at this time. DAPT until 10/2024, then aspirin alone. Return in 3-4 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - nosebleeds
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Nosebleeds for about 6 weeks, now a few times a week, usually waking at night or first thing in the morning, mostly from the right but sometimes either side. Stop with 10 minutes of pinching. No blood in stool, no gum bleeding beyond the usual, no black stools. On aspirin + clopidogrel until October. Uses CPAP nightly with the humidifier set low because the tubing gets wet.

O: Vitals as charted. Nares: dried blood and crusting anteriorly bilaterally, no active bleeding, no visible mass. Oropharynx clear. No petechiae.

A/P: Recurrent anterior epistaxis on dual antiplatelet therapy with dry mucosa from CPAP. Not stopping antiplatelets, stent is under a year. CBC, PT/INR and liver panel today (lithium level as well since due). Saline spray during the day, petroleum-based ointment inside the nostrils at night, try the humidifier one notch higher. ENT referral to look for a vessel worth cauterizing.

documents.title: Bleeding workup
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC normal including platelets and hemoglobin, PT/INR normal, liver panel normal. Lithium 0.8. Nothing systemic. ENT appointment is 9/23. Message sent to patient.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology, 09/23/2024. Referred by primary care.

HPI: Two months of nosebleeds, mostly overnight or on waking, increasing in frequency, controlled with pressure. Seen by cardiology recently; on aspirin and clopidogrel after a 2023 coronary stent, clopidogrel due to stop next month. Uses CPAP for sleep apnea, about a year now.

PMH: CAD with stent, HTN, hyperlipidemia, bipolar I on lithium, nephrogenic DI, OSA, colon cancer s/p right hemicolectomy. NKDA. Never smoker.

BP 138/86.
Exam: External nose straight. Anterior rhinoscopy shows dry, crusted mucosa over the anterior septum with a little fresh blood; no prominent single vessel, no septal deformity, no polyps or mass. Oral cavity and oropharynx normal. Neck without adenopathy.
Primary care labs in August: CBC, coagulation studies and liver tests normal.

Impression: localized idiopathic anterior epistaxis from mucosal drying, likely aggravated by CPAP airflow and antiplatelet therapy.
Plan: Turn the CPAP heated humidifier up and use heated tubing; saline gel to each nostril at bedtime and on waking; avoid digital trauma. No cautery today since no discrete vessel. Pressure technique reviewed. Return if bleeding continues after clopidogrel is stopped.

Next visit in one year.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, 03/25/2025.

Routine visit. History of NSTEMI with mid-LAD stent (10/2023) and stable angina in early 2024, quiet since the medication changes that spring. No chest pressure, dyspnea or palpitations. Takes everything as prescribed. Never smoker; eats a careful diet. He asks whether anything else would lower his chance of another heart attack.

Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, NTG prn; lithium and amiloride per his other physicians. NKDA.

BP 132/84. Exam unremarkable.
Lipids 03/11/2025 (primary care): LDL 98, HDL 45, triglycerides 150.

Assessment: CAD with prior MI, LDL above goal for secondary prevention.
Plan: We discussed adding ezetimibe to his statin, which lowers LDL further and has reduced recurrent cardiac events when added to statin therapy, with few side effects. He agrees. Start ezetimibe 10 mg daily. Continue the rest. Repeat lipids in 2-3 months (can be drawn with primary care). Return in one year.

documents.title: RE: New cholesterol pill

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, 61.

A quiet year, which he says he has earned. No angina for a year. Cardiology added ezetimibe in March. No nosebleeds since January. CPAP nightly. Nocturia once. Mood even, saw psychiatry in November. Colon: 2-year CT and CEA clear in February.

Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30, atorvastatin 40, ezetimibe 10, lisinopril 20, lithium 300 bid, amiloride 5, NTG prn. NKDA.
Social: same job, thinking about retiring at 65. Never smoker, social drinker.

Exam: vitals as charted. Nares without crusting. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Neuro nonfocal, no tremor. Affect bright. PHQ-9 2.

A/P
1. CAD/prior MI/stable angina: asymptomatic. Lipids today on statin plus ezetimibe.
2. Epistaxis: resolved with humidification; off the active list.
3. HTN controlled.
4. Lithium/NDI: lithium, CMP, TSH today.
5. OSA, colon cancer surveillance, as above.
6. Prevention: up to date; flu and COVID in the fall.

RTC 3-4 months for lithium follow-up.

events.reason: Sudden painless vision loss, left eye

conditions.label: Unspecified retinal detachment with retinal break, left eye

documents.title: Emergency department record - vision loss
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 09/22/2025, arrival 15:10.

CC: lost vision in the left eye.

HPI: 61-year-old man with CAD (prior MI, LAD stent), stage IIA colon cancer s/p right hemicolectomy, and a cardiology visit this spring. About 45 minutes before arrival, while at his desk, a dark shadow suddenly covered the lower half of the vision in his left eye, painless, and it has since spread over most of that eye's field. No headache, nausea, double vision, eye pain or light sensitivity. No injury. Never had anything like it. No known eye disease. Blood pressure and cholesterol have been well controlled.

PMH: CAD s/p PCI, stable angina, HTN, hyperlipidemia, bipolar I on lithium, nephrogenic DI, OSA on CPAP, colon cancer.
PSH: right hemicolectomy; colonoscopy with polypectomy.
Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30, atorvastatin 40, ezetimibe 10, lisinopril 20, lithium carbonate 300 twice daily, amiloride 5, NTG prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol, office manager.
Family: father MI at 55, mother type 2 diabetes, paternal uncle stroke at 60, maternal grandfather colon polyps.

Exam: vitals as charted, comfortable. Right eye acuity normal; left eye acuity reduced. Left pupil sluggish to light. Intraocular pressure normal both eyes. Extraocular movements full both eyes. Conjunctivae quiet. Neuro otherwise nonfocal.

Ophthalmology consulted from the ED: dilated fundus examination of the left eye shows a retinal detachment with a retinal break; right eye normal.

Impression: left rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.
Disposition: discharged to the care of the on-call retina surgeon for repair tomorrow morning. Nothing by mouth after midnight. Continue home meds including aspirin unless the surgeon advises otherwise.

medications.sig: 1 drop in the left eye four times daily, taper over 4 weeks
1 drop in the left eye four times daily for 1 week

documents.title: Retina surgery - left eye
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside retina practice. Operative summary 09/23/2025.
Preoperative diagnosis: rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, left eye.
Procedure: 23-gauge pars plana vitrectomy, endolaser to the retinal break, fluid-air exchange and gas tamponade, left eye. Monitored anesthesia care with retrobulbar block. Aspirin continued.
Findings: retinal detachment with a single retinal break, flattened under air; laser applied around the break.
No complications.
Postoperative: head positioning as instructed for 5 days. No air travel or high altitude, and no nitrous oxide anesthesia, while gas remains (about 6-8 weeks); green gas band placed on the left wrist. Prednisolone acetate 1% and moxifloxacin 0.5% drops four times daily. Follow-up tomorrow, 1 week and 1 month.

documents.title: Check-in after eye surgery
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after we received the ED and retina records. Day 3 after vitrectomy for left retinal detachment. Doing the positioning, mild ache controlled with acetaminophen, using both drops. Vision in that eye is blurry through the gas bubble as expected. Taking his heart meds and lithium as usual. Reminded no NSAIDs with lithium. Post-ED visit with PCP 10/7.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit and retina surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - after retinal detachment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen two weeks after the ED visit (9/22) for sudden painless vision loss in the left eye, a rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, repaired by vitrectomy with gas the next morning. One-week retina check said the retina is attached. Gas bubble shrinking, can see the line moving. Drops tapering. Wearing the gas wristband; no flying planned.

Otherwise well. No chest pressure. Lithium 0.9 in August. Mood fine, a bit frustrated about not driving for a couple of weeks.

Exam: vitals as charted. Left eye mildly injected, no discharge. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
1. Left retinal detachment s/p repair: retina following. Told him to call the retina office immediately for any new shadow, flashes or floaters in either eye. If he ever needs surgery while gas remains, anesthesia must know (no nitrous).
2. CAD, HTN, lipids: stable, no change.
3. Bipolar/lithium: next level in the winter.
4. Flu and COVID today.

RTC January.

documents.title: Psychiatry annual visit
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, 10/29/2025. Bipolar I disorder in sustained remission on lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily. Coped well with eye surgery in September. Euthymic, no psychotic or manic symptoms, sleeping well. No tremor. Recent levels 0.8-0.9. Continue current dose. Return in one year.

documents.title: Retina follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Outside retina practice, 11/19/2025. Eight weeks after left pars plana vitrectomy, endolaser and gas for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment. Gas fully resorbed. Retina attached 360 degrees with laser scar around the treated break. Visual acuity left eye 20/50, right eye normal. Intraocular pressure normal. Drops finished. Activity unrestricted; may fly. Return in 3 months, sooner for new flashes, floaters or shadow.
